h1: The 5 Best Lawn Mowers Under $300 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lawn Mowers Under $300 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five lawn mowers under $300, from 18-inch gas and cordless to manual reel models, with advice on which fits your yard.
summary: The PowerSmart EasyCut 18-inch gas mower is our top pick for small to medium yards. The Wild Badger 40V cordless is the best way to skip fuel entirely. The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 is the cheapest and simplest option for a small flat lawn.
intro: A cheap mower rarely fails on power. It fails because the buyer picked the wrong kind of mower for the yard: a reel on thick grass, a narrow deck on a big lot, or a battery model with no plan for a second battery.

We ranked five mowers that sit well below the $300 ceiling, using the spec sheet and the way owners describe them. Cutting width, power source, upkeep and how much work each one asks of you drove the order, since those decide whether a budget mower feels like a bargain or a chore.

products.name: PowerSmart EasyCut 18-Inch Gas Lawn Mower
products.verdict: Gas-mower cutting width at a price that leaves room in the budget.
products.description:
The EasyCut has an 18-inch deck, side discharge and a 144cc four-cycle gas engine. It has five height positions, so you can step down gradually after a long gap between mows. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It ranks above the other PowerSmart because the listing gives a clearer feature set, including the height range, and above the cordless Wild Badger because there is no battery to run out halfway through. The trade is routine engine upkeep, with fuel, oil and the occasional spark plug.

Choose it for a small to medium yard where you want to finish in one go. The caveat is noise and maintenance, and an 18-inch deck is narrower than the 21-inch class.
products.idealFor: Small to medium yards where finishing in one pass matters.
products.skipIf: You do not want to handle fuel or engine maintenance.

products.name: PowerSmart 18-Inch 144cc Gas Lawn Mower
products.verdict: Same class of mower as the top pick when that model is out of stock.
products.description:
This PowerSmart pairs an 18-inch deck with a 144cc gas engine, side discharge and push drive. It also sits in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It ranks just below the EasyCut because the listing details fewer adjustments, such as no stated height range, so there is less to confirm before buying. In practice the two are close, and this one is the fallback when the first is unavailable.

It suits buyers who want gas power and nothing more. The caveat is the same upkeep and noise as any gas mower, plus a push drive that you steer and power yourself.
products.idealFor: Anyone wanting the top pick's class when it is out of stock.
products.skipIf: You want self-propelled drive or a mulching setup.

products.name: Wild Badger Power 40V 18-Inch Brushless Cordless Lawn Mower
products.verdict: Gas-width deck with none of the fuel or cord hassle.
products.description:
The Wild Badger uses a 40V brushless motor in an 18-inch deck, runs on battery with no cord, and sits in the $100 to $200 bucket. No fuel and no oil changes is the headline benefit.

It ranks below the gas picks because battery runtime caps how much grass you can cut on one charge, and above the reel mowers because you do not do the pushing power yourself. The tradeoff is runtime against upkeep.

Buy it if your yard is small to medium and you hate engine maintenance. The caveat is that you should check the battery details on the listing, since a larger lawn may need a second pack.
products.idealFor: Small to medium yards where quiet, low-upkeep mowing matters.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is large or the grass is thick and tall.

products.name: LawnMaster LMRM1602 16-Inch 5-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.verdict: A manual reel with a wider cut and zero running costs.
products.description:
The LawnMaster is a manual reel mower with a 16-inch, five-blade cylinder that needs no fuel, cord or battery. It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It ranks above the American Lawn Mower because the cut is two inches wider, which shortens each pass, and below the powered picks because you provide all the power. The five-blade cylinder also gives a finer cut than a three-blade design would.

It suits a small, flat lawn kept short on a regular schedule. The caveat is that reel mowers struggle with overgrown grass, sticks and uneven ground.
products.idealFor: Small flat lawns mowed often and kept short.
products.skipIf: Your grass gets long between mows or the yard is bumpy.

products.name: American Lawn Mower 1204-14 14-Inch 4-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.verdict: The simplest, lowest-cost way to keep a tiny lawn trimmed.
products.description:
This reel mower has a 14-inch, four-blade manual design with no fuel, cord or battery. It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket, the lowest on this list.

It ranks last because the narrow cut means more passes than any other mower here. Against the LawnMaster, the width is the real tradeoff, since two inches less per pass adds up over a lawn.

It works for a small, flat patch where you want the lowest cost and the least upkeep. The caveat is that it is not for large lawns, tall grass or anyone who dislikes pushing.
products.idealFor: Tiny flat lawns and buyers who want the lowest cost.
products.skipIf: You have more than a small patch of grass.

whatMatters.detail: Deck width is how much grass you cut per pass. An 18-inch deck finishes a lawn faster than a 14-inch one. Check the inch figure in the title and compare it against your lawn size.
Gas gives unlimited runtime, battery gives quiet and no fuel, and a reel needs only your effort. Each suits a different yard. Look for engine cc or battery voltage in the listing.
Height positions let you raise the deck after a long gap and lower it later. This prevents scalping. Look for a stated number of positions.
Gas engines need oil and fuel, batteries age, and reel blades need occasional adjustment. This ongoing cost matters more than the sticker price. Check what the listing says is included.
Reel mowers suit small, flat, regularly cut lawns. Larger or rougher yards need a motor. Measure your lawn before you buy.

faq.q: Can a reel mower handle thick grass?
faq.a: Not well. Reel mowers cut best when grass is kept short and mowed often. If your lawn grows quickly, the PowerSmart gas models are a better fit.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with a budget mower?
faq.a: Buying a narrow deck for a large yard. Every inch of width saves passes, so match the deck to the lawn.

faq.q: Is gas still worth it over battery?
faq.a: For bigger or tougher lawns, yes, because there is no runtime cap. Battery makes sense for small yards and quiet streets.
Most arrive partly assembled and need handle setup. Check the listing for what is included before buying.

faq.q: How do I maintain a reel mower?
faq.a: Keep the blades clean and occasionally adjust the blade contact. There is no fuel, oil or spark plug to deal with.

faq.q: Will a cordless mower cover my whole lawn?
faq.a: That depends on lawn size and battery capacity. If the lawn is bigger than small, plan for a second battery or pick a gas model.

finalTake: For most yards under $300, the PowerSmart EasyCut is the practical choice. The Wild Badger 40V suits anyone who wants to skip fuel. Reel mowers are the right answer only for small, flat, well-kept lawns, with the LawnMaster giving the wider cut.
